extracted.intended_audience: Academic authors preparing a revise-and-resubmit response to journal peer review (researchers, graduate students, and coauthors)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing a structured, professional response-to-reviewers (revise-and-resubmit) letter that maps reviewer reports to concrete manuscript revisions, justifies decisions, and makes it easy for editors and reviewers to verify changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short overview of major changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a concise overview that lists the main revisions, including new analyses, restructured sections, or added controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the most significant changes in one or two sentences or a short bullet list with three to six items, each pointing to sections or figures. This prepares reviewers and editors for the detailed responses that follow and anchors the revise-and-resubmit response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete point-by-point structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Quote the full set of reviews and respond to each numbered comment in turn, rather than selecting only a subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat every comment as deserving a visible response. Organize responses by reviewer and number comments consistently so editors can match each reviewer comment to a clear response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear links between comments and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the editor exactly where each change appears (for example by providing page and line numbers or brief quotations of revised text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide page and line references or short quoted snippets of revised text so reviewers can confirm changes quickly instead of searching the entire manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional, measured tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use polite, respectful language and keep emotional reactions out of the response document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the reviewers' work, express appreciation, and maintain a consistent, neutral tone even when disagreeing. Politeness helps reviewers stay open to your arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of prioritisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish 'essential' from 'unessential' requests and show you prioritized major issues over minor ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate comments into 'suggested actions' and log which actions you took. Use the opening summary to highlight major revisions driven by essential requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer the editor's three questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your letter answer: What were the main concerns? What did you change in response? Where can the reviewer find those changes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the letter so these three questions are clear up front (summary) and supported by the point-by-point responses with references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare before responding (read, pause, then plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read all reports once, pause for a day or two to separate emotion from substance, then plan revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the pause, share reports with coauthors or trusted colleagues to identify main concerns and areas of agreement/disagreement before drafting responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map reviewer comments into an actionable table
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a spreadsheet/table with columns for reviewer, comment number, comment text (copied verbatim), category, planned action, and location in revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this table to assign responsibilities, track dependencies, and generate the point-by-point responses and page/line references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify comments into four categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Label each comment as one of: major conceptual or methodological issues; clarification and explanation issues; infeasible or out-of-scope requests; minor issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the categories to decide what belongs in the opening summary (major issues), what to handle concisely (clarifications/minor), and how to justify not-implementing infeasible requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a predictable, scannable response letter structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Include salutation, opening paragraph (thank you, decision reference, 1–2 sentence summary), summary of major revisions, point-by-point responses, and a closing paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A predictable format helps editors and reviewers skim under time pressure. Keep the summary short and the point-by-point section clearly organized by reviewer and comment number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-by-point response components
rubrics_metrics.description: For each comment: label the comment, quote it verbatim, state your overall stance (agree/clarify/disagree), describe the action taken, and give page/line references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open responses with neutral phrases (e.g., 'We thank the reviewer and agree that...'). Link major issues back to the opening summary. Keep clarification and minor responses concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote comments exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy the reviewer comment exactly, including emphasis, to avoid disputes about what was said.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoting verbatim prevents misunderstanding and makes it clear which text you are responding to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label every comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a consistent label format (e.g., 'Reviewer 2, comment 4') for each item in the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent labels make it easy for editors and reviewers to cross-reference between the review reports and your responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to every comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure every reviewer comment has a matching response in your letter, even if the change is small or you decline the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to respond to comments can be seen as ignoring reviewers. For small issues, a concise acknowledgement and reference to the fix is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link responses to the summary for major issues
rubrics_metrics.description: For major conceptual or methodological changes, explicitly connect the point-by-point response to the broader revisions summarized in the opening section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows coherence between detailed responses and the manuscript-level changes editors most care about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the conflict in your own words, identify what the editor needs to know, seek internal consensus, and explain your defensible choice in the responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address each reviewer separately (e.g., explain to Reviewer 1 why you kept a section long while to Reviewer 2 describe clarifications added). Consider a short, factual note to the editor if the conflict is sharp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling infeasible or out-of-scope requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge the value of the suggestion, explain why you cannot implement it for this manuscript (e.g., new data, new grant required), and strengthen the Limitations section to reflect the constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being transparent about constraints and noting future work addresses concerns without overpromising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete language patterns for tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt ready-made phrasing for agreement, clarification, and respectful disagreement to keep responses neutral and scientific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: 'We thank the reviewer... We have revised...' for agreement; 'We apologize for the lack of clarity... We have rewritten...' for clarification; 'After careful consideration, we decided not to implement... because...' for disagreement. These keep focus on the science rather than personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow for revise-and-resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a repeatable workflow: Decision received → Mapping and planning → Revising the manuscript (major issues first) → Drafting the response letter → Cross-checking and polishing → Final submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address major conceptual/methodological issues first, log changes to enable page/line references, verify every claimed change appears, and keep the table/letter as a template for future submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that every reviewer comment has a matching response and that every claimed change in the letter appears in the revised manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the full rebuttal letter in one pass to check tone and coherence. Confirm page and line references are correct before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission review to anticipate likely reviewer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pre-submission review (colleagues, writing groups, or structured tools) to catch common problems before journal peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-submission feedback can identify unclear research questions, poor writing/presentation, incomplete or poorly reported analyses, untidy tables/figures, and underdeveloped discussions—issues that often trigger major revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion-level pre-submission feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Use structured pre-submission tools to get criterion-level diagnostics similar to reviewer categories (e.g., interpretation of evidence, presentation, tables/figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such feedback can quote problematic sentences and recommend analytical moves, flag unsupported conclusions, and suggest concrete fixes for tables and figures before journal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table and figure presentation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure tables/figures are properly referenced, layout and labelling make data easy to read, and entries/percentages/abbreviations are consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific revision tasks include adding multi-level headers, defining abbreviations, adding totals and denominators, and ensuring tables are referenced in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a reusable template and logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the comments table and the response letter as templates for future submissions and to streamline subsequent rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logging changes and reusing templates makes future revise-and-resubmit cycles faster and more consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability and scanability for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your response document predictable and easy to scan so editors can quickly match reviewer comments to your responses and manuscript changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent formatting, numbered lists, and short summaries so busy editors can evaluate the response efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate comments into 'suggested actions' and log decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert reviewer remarks into explicit revision tasks and record whether you implemented them, partially implemented them, or declined with justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit log demonstrates that you engaged seriously with each suggestion and shows the rationale for your decisions.
